design_note: Inspects a paused thread against a renamed node in a candidate graph. The compatibility failure shows why valid stored state and an owned thread do not make deployment migration safe.

source.title: Graph API overview
source.concept: Interrupted threads may still refer to pending node names. Renaming or removing those nodes can break continuation; technically compatible changes can also need separate business-logic review.
source.scope: Original graph versions and pending node; the application gate is illustrative, not a new LangGraph API or automatic migration guarantee.

lesson.title: The saved node must still have somewhere to run
lesson.intro: ShopAssist thread T-61 paused at approval_wait in graph G-4. Candidate G-5 removes that node and introduces review_card. Its deployment check inspects the old checkpoint before permitting continuation.

data.name: Paused thread T-61
data.result: Keep T-61 on compatible behavior or migrate explicitly.

read: The checkpoint is intact and belongs to the right tenant.
G-5 still cannot resume the named pending node.
Deployment compatibility and business approval require different evidence.
lesson.question: Can the operator safely fix this by editing approval_wait to review_card in the checkpoint?
lesson.answer: That edit alone does not prove safe continuation. The new node may interpret state or approval differently. Use the compatible behavior version or a tested migration that preserves the proposal, pending work, budgets and effect identity. Revalidate current authority before any effect; changing graph state cannot create permission.
lesson.takeaway: Test stored pending work against the next graph, including the business meaning of continuation.
lesson.assumption: Fictional application compatibility gate; no automatic state rewrite occurs. Ordinary behavior pinning never overrides current emergency restrictions.
